issues.legal_issue: A challenge to a Collector’s eviction orders may proceed through special-leave appeals and constitutional petitions where the maintainability objection is unsupported.
material_facts: The civil appeals challenged the Collector’s orders directing the occupants to hand over land.
The occupants also filed constitutional petitions challenging the Collector’s power to dispossess them.
The State raised a preliminary objection to the appeals’ maintainability but cited no authority supporting it.
issues.conclusion: The preliminary objection was overruled, and the appeals and constitutional petitions were entertained.
issues.legal_principle: The Court rejected the maintainability objection because no authority had been cited to support it and because the constitutional petitions also challenged the alleged deprivation of the occupants’ rights to remain in possession until dispossessed according to law. The proceedings were brought under Articles 136 and 32 of the Constitution.

predicates.special_leave_appeal_challenges_collecto: A party has brought a special-leave appeal challenging an order made by a Collector.
predicates.constitutional_petition_challenges_colle: A party has brought a constitutional petition challenging the Collector’s power to dispossess it.
predicates.maintainability_objection_lacks_supporti: The party objecting to maintainability has cited no authority supporting the objection.

issues.definition: When a special-leave appeal or constitutional petition challenges a Collector’s order or power and the maintainability objection lacks supporting authority, the challenge proceedings are maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: A Collector cannot order eviction under a statutory land-utilization regime while the applicability of that regime and the occupants’ status under it remain disputed and undetermined.
material_facts: No lease or Patta was produced for the land in dispute.
The occupants denied that the land had been allotted to them under the statute relied on for eviction, and the parties disputed the basis on which the land had been allotted.

The orders assumed that the occupants had received leases for a fixed term and that the persons to whom the land was to be returned remained its owners, but those matters had not been established by a court decision.
The State filed an affidavit indicating that some of the land vested in village panchayats.
The Collector ordered the occupants to hand over the land without first resolving the disputed source and extent of the Collector’s authority.
issues.conclusion: The eviction orders were quashed. The Collector was to investigate whether the State had taken possession under the statute and whether valid leases had been executed, whether compensation proceedings affected the alleged owners’ rights, what rights the occupants might have through long possession if no valid leases existed, the panchayats’ claims, and whether the Collector could act or the claims should be resolved in other proceedings. No further proceedings under the statute could be taken against the occupants until it was determined that the land remained governed by it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4 and 5 of the East Punjab Utilization of Lands Act, 1949, the Act’s eviction provisions apply only where it is clear or undisputed that the person to be evicted was a lessee under Section 5. Although the Act does not empower the Collector to adjudicate questions of right and title where those questions properly arise, the Collector must determine the source and extent of the Collector’s power and jurisdiction when they are challenged, including whether the Act applies at all. The Court distinguished Dasaudha Singh and Others v. State of Haryana and Others and Haryana Co-operative Multipurpose Society v. Collector of Kaithal because those cases did not involve a dispute about the enactment under which admitted leases had been granted.

rule.if: collector_eviction_proceeding and lease_status_uncertain and statutory_basis_uncertain and ownership_or_possession_claims_contested and eviction_order_precedes_jurisdictional_inquiry

predicates.collector_eviction_proceeding: An authority is conducting a proceeding to evict occupants from land.
predicates.lease_status_uncertain: The occupants’ status as lessees under the asserted legal regime has not been established or is disputed.
predicates.statutory_basis_uncertain: The legal regime under which the land was taken or allotted has not been established or is disputed.
predicates.ownership_or_possession_claims_contested: The parties or other claimants dispute who owns the land or what rights arise from the occupants’ possession.
predicates.eviction_order_precedes_jurisdictional_i: The authority orders eviction before determining whether the asserted legal regime governs the land and authorizes its action.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding involves uncertain lease status and statutory basis, contested ownership or possession claims, and an eviction order made before jurisdiction is examined, the eviction order is quashed and further action under the asserted regime is deferred until its applicability is determined.
